topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: Well, the miller’s son was tellin’ me o’ a place in the next town where they’d make a stew so rich, it’d warm yer bones better'n a hearth fire on a winter’s eve. But now, come to hear it’s to be no more, it does leave a pang in the heart. I’ve never set foot past the hills yonder myself, but to think of such good fare being no more... it’s like the first frost nipping at the buds, cutting them before their time. One can’t help but wonder, what becomes of all the laughter and the joy that place held within its walls? But the fields lie fallow for a time, and then, there is always the promise of a new sowing. Mayhaps, there’s a future where another good place rises from the soil, to feed the folk and fill their spirits.
